original_question: For fixed integers k and p, does there exist a constant c = c(k,p) such that every k-uniform hypergraph in which every set of p edges has nonempty common intersection (that is, the (p,p)-property) has transversal number strictly less than c?
target_in_paper: No exact match. arXiv:0902.4207 is a survey on quadratic stochastic operators, not a hypergraph/transversal paper; the closest official statement in the paper is Section 3, Problem 2: define transversality for an arbitrary QSO and characterize, in terms of its coefficient matrix, when the QSO is transversal.
correct_elements: The draft is mathematically coherent on its own, but it does not match the paper's subject. The paper does not discuss k-uniform hypergraphs, the (p,p)-property, or bounded transversal numbers. The only superficial overlap is the word "transversal," which in the paper refers to a property of quadratic stochastic operators via an associated skew-symmetric matrix.
missing_details: The ambient object in the paper is a quadratic stochastic operator V:S^{m-1}->S^{m-1}, not a hypergraph.
The paper defines a QSO by heredity coefficients p_{ij,k} satisfying p_{ij,k}=p_{ji,k}>=0 and sum_k p_{ij,k}=1 for all i,j.
The nearby context is specifically about Volterra QSOs, which satisfy p_{ij,k}=0 whenever k is not one of the parents i,j.
For Volterra QSOs, the operator is written via a skew-symmetric matrix A=(a_{ki}); "transversal" means that all even-order principal minors of A are nonzero.

Problem 2 asks for a definition of transversality for arbitrary QSOs and necessary and sufficient conditions on the coefficient matrix for transversality; it does not ask for existence of a constant bound.
The parameters k and p from the draft do not correspond to any variables in the paper's target problem.
The paper is organized around numbered theorems/problems on QSOs; it does not contain a hypergraph Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3 matching the draft.
refined_question: For a general quadratic stochastic operator V:S^{m-1}->S^{m-1} with heredity coefficients (p_{ij,k}), define a notion of transversality that extends the Volterra case—where a Volterra QSO is called transversal when its associated skew-symmetric matrix has all even-order principal minors nonzero—and determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the coefficient matrix of V under which V is transversal.
justification: The supplied draft does not correspond to the contents of arXiv:0902.4207. The paper's title, abstract, introduction, and Section 2 show that its subject is quadratic stochastic operators on the simplex, and Section 3 contains the nearest official open problem, Problem 2, which asks to extend and characterize "transversality" for arbitrary QSOs. I therefore used Section 3, Problem 2, together with the QSO definition from Section 2 and the Volterra-transversality definition immediately preceding Problem 2, as the closest paper-faithful target.
